Assume µ = 0. (i) If F ⪰∗ W0 (F is DFRA), and for the first zero x∗ of fr,γ1:r,0 − fq,β1:q,0 on (0, 1) we have Zr,γ1:r,0,0(−ln(1−x∗)) − Zq,β1:q,0,0(−ln(1−x∗)) ≤ 0, then Xr,γ1:r,0 ⪯ss Xq,β1:q,0. (ii) If −β1:q < α ≠ 0, F ⪰∗ Wα (F is α-DGFRA), and the analogous Z-condition at (1−(1−x∗)^α)/α holds, then Xr,γ1:r,0 ⪯ss Xq,β1:q,0. 2. Take now µ > 0. (i)-(ii) analogous ⇒ Xr,γ1:r,0 ⪯ss Xq,β1:q,0 (as printed).

records.quote: Theorem 1. Let H be a family of nondecreasing functions that is closed under compositions. Let Xr,γ̃r and Yq,β̃q denote the r-th and q-th GOS based on parameters γ̃r = (γ1, . . . , γr) and β̃r = (β1, . . . , βq), respectively, and baseline distribution functions F and G, respectively.
